A consent agenda item for the sale of surplus property at Fauntleroy Way No. 5 was approved and advanced to full council on an expedited basis. The proposed ordinance 20260108 authorizes the sale of 39.1 acres of agricultural land in Townsville District 9, previously held by King County Water and Land Resources Division (Willard), declared surplus on September 8th, 2021, following a F M D surplus declaration analysis. The property was appraised at $600,000 using a sales comparison approach among five land transactions, with the purchase and sale agreement including a reserved agricultural easement; proceeds will support Willard’s acquisition of new open space and recreation facility improvements. The minutes from June 10th were approved by unanimous vote (five ayes, zero noes), with Councilmember Mosqueda excused. Public comment was closed due to no attendees signing in or joining online. A consent agenda item for the sale of surplus property at Fauntleroy Way No. 5 was approved and advanced to full council on an expedited basis. The proposed ordinance 20260108 authorizes the sale of 39.1 acres of agricultural land in Townsville District 9, previously held by King County Water and Land Resources Division (Willard), declared surplus on September 8th, 2021, following a F M D surplus declaration analysis. The property was appraised at $600,000 using a sales comparison approach among five land transactions, with the purchase and sale agreement including a reserved agricultural easement; proceeds will support Willard’s acquisition of new open space and recreation facility improvements. The meeting discusses a restrictive covenant requiring agricultural land preservation for thirty years due to conditions set by the State DNR when receiving the property, though no explanation is provided for why it is not perpetual. Council Member Perry raises a question about whether DNR intends to later utilize the property during an interim period and requests offline feedback on this potential use case. A motion is made by Council Member Barone to give a do-pass recommendation to propose Ordinance 20260108, with Amendment One extending the contingency date for council action; the amendment passes unanimously (5 ayes, 0 noes) with Mosqueda excused.
